title: Practice: will, going to, or present continuous?

questions.prompt: Complete with be going to: "I ___ buy a new dictionary."
questions.explanation: With I, be going to is "am going to" + base verb: I am going to buy a new dictionary. "is going to" is the form for he / she / it; "going to" alone drops "am"; "am go to" loses the -ing of "going".

questions.prompt: Choose the future word that turns this sentence into a planned action: "They are joining the basketball team ___."
questions.explanation: A planned action needs am / is / are + verb + ing + a FUTURE word: they are joining the team tomorrow. "yesterday" and "last week" point to the past; "every day" describes a habit, not a plan for one moment in the future.

questions.prompt: Complete: "In the future, cars ___ smart cards instead of keys."
questions.explanation: The future tense is will + bare infinitive, the same with every subject: cars will have smart cards. After will the verb never takes -s ("will has"), never "to" ("will to have") and never -ing ("will having").

questions.prompt: What does this sentence express? "Our teacher is giving us a test tomorrow."
questions.explanation: is + giving is the present progressive, and "tomorrow" is a future word: together they express a planned action. It is not an intention, because there is no going to + base verb; it is not happening now, because the future word "tomorrow" moves it to the future; and nothing in it is finished.

questions.prompt: Complete the question: "What ___ you intend to do after the exam?"
questions.explanation: intend is an ordinary verb in the present, so its questions use do / does; with "you" it is do: What do you intend to do? "does" is for he / she / it; "are" and "is" belong to be going to or be thinking of, not to intend.

questions.prompt: Turn this intention into a planned action: "We are going to visit London."

options.text: We are visiting London next week.
We are going to visiting London.
We will visiting London next week.

questions.explanation: A planned action is am / is / are + verb + ing + a future word: we are visiting London next week. "We visit London next week" uses the simple present; "are going to visiting" puts -ing after going to, which needs a base verb; "will visiting" puts -ing after will, which needs a bare infinitive.
